title: ADR 0002: lane-aware shell authority for sub-agents
description:
# ADR 0002 — Lane-aware shell authority for sub-agents

**Status:** Proposed, pending acceptance (implementation + tests).

## Decision

The shell decision in sub-agent dispatches becomes a function of the **actual
dispatch world**, not of the tool name alone. yaah's supervisor
`destructive_guard` currently denies `bash` / `powershell` /
`background_process` by name in every sub-agent scope
(`internal/agent/supervision/service.go:127`), through a check whose signature
is `(ownerID, toolName, argsJSON)` (`internal/agent/pipeline/supervisor_guard.go:35`)
— it has no world, lane or realm input, so it cannot tell a host shell from a
container shell.

The distinction matters because the two lanes put the shell in different
places: a worktree-lane shell is a host process at the host uid behind a
possibly-absent Landlock jail (`internal/tools/workspace.go:326,344`;
`internal/agent/runner/runner.go:1339`, and `:1776,1784` refuse restrictive
grants without a jail), while a container-lane shell executes in-band inside
the croft world (`internal/tools/dispatch_container.go:135`; `ws.Exec` at
`internal/tools/bash.go:76`), where the only reachable host surfaces are the
shaped rw binds plus read-only secret mounts, and the only host write path is
approval-gated `apply_out`.

Policy in short: worktree lane unchanged (denied); container lane permitted
when the actual world is a container, network posture is `deny_all` or
broker-mediated (never `host`), and resource limits are set; degraded worlds
fail closed; `background_process` stays denied in both lanes; no command
allowlist; config defaults to deny with an explicit opt-in.

## Prerequisites (gates, in order)

- P1 — default seccomp profile + `NoNewPrivileges` in croft's spec opts.
- P2 — mandatory pids/memory limits for sub-agent container worlds
  (`Config.Limits` already carries pids via `withLinuxResources`).
- P3 — refuse `Network: host` for sub-agent container worlds at the
  `sandbox/croft` lowering seam; broker or none only.
- P4 — bounded exec output inside the sandbox (yaah truncates the transcript,
  not the sandbox-side buffer).

## Implementation

yaah binds the resolved world into the guard middleware
(`pipeline/config.go:269`), splits the policy by lane, adds a table test over
{worktree, container, container-degraded} × {bash, powershell,
background_process}, and updates the go:embed'd model-facing docs (the
`doc_parity_test.go` gate pins schema/doc agreement, so behaviour and docs must
move together; epic yaah-c3z3 tracks the container-lane prompt deficit).

## Rejected

Global disable of the rule; a read-only command allowlist (a shell executes
what a matcher cannot see); expressing the allowance as tool omission
(omission means "cannot work here", refusal means "must not be used here");
allowing shell in both lanes and relying on the jail; per-role shell config
(a second authority vocabulary competing with grants); implementing in
croft/goatherd (only yaah holds both world and sub-agent scope).

## Open questions

Secrets withheld from shell-bearing roles vs P3 sufficiency; whether a
container-lane shell can reach the session container (not just the dispatch
world); `apply_out` remaining the sole host write path once arbitrary commands
run in the world — worth a probe-first canary.

## Record

`croft/docs/adr/0002-lane-aware-shell-authority.md`

title: States(ctx): enumerate pinned states for crash recovery and orphan pruning
description:
# States(ctx): enumerate pinned states for crash recovery and orphan pruning

## Context

Captured states are pinned under the namespace `croft-states` lease
(`pinState`, `sandbox.go:740`) and live until `ReleaseState` or namespace
teardown. No expiry is the *right* default for the settlement horizon (a
proposal under human review must never be GC'd mid-decision) — but there is
no way to **discover** states either:

- A host that crashes between `Capture` and its settlement decision orphans a
  pinned state forever (until namespace teardown). Nothing in croft can find
  it again.
- croft-broker maintains its own SQLite registry of states precisely because
  the substrate can't list its own — every host currently has to rebuild that
  bookkeeping outside croft.

Shepherd's analog: retained outputs are pinned under enumerable refs, and
hosts prune orphans after crashes (yaah's `yaah shepherd prune` for worktrees).
The substrate should provide the listing primitive the hosts build on.

## Plan

1. Add a state-enumeration surface, e.g.
   `States(ctx context.Context) ([]WorkspaceState, error)`.
   - Go interface-growth note: adding a method to the public `Sandbox`
     interface is a breaking change for implementors. Prefer either a new
     optional capability interface (the runtime's `DeltaApplier` pattern) or a
     standalone constructor-level function — decide in implementation.
2. Implementation: list snapshots pinned under the `croft-states` lease;
   parse the `croft/<id>/{active,committed}/<n>` labels for lineage (sandbox
   id, layer kind, sequence); return `WorkspaceState` values with the same
   shape hosts hand around.
3. Docs recipe: "audit and prune orphans" — enumerate, compare against the
   host's (or the trace's) expected live outputs, `ReleaseState` the rest.

## Acceptance

- Unit (fake leases): states listed after captures; listing reflects
  `ReleaseState` and namespace teardown.
- Live test simulating the crash case: destroy a sandbox without releasing →
  its pinned states remain enumerable → releasable.
- croft-broker's registry can be reconstructed (or cross-checked) from
  `States()` alone.
- Docs recipe added to `docs/overview.md`.

## References

- yaah bead `yaah-kit` (container-lane seam work; recovery story depends on this)
- `croft-shepherd-fit.md` §7-8 (Frameworks dir) — gap analysis
- goatherd-runtime `recovery.go` ("the trace is the registry") — the host-side
  counterpart that needs a substrate-side listing to reconcile against

title: Digest-stable state identity: no-change capture fast path + expose the differ's content digest
description:
# Digest-stable state identity: no-change capture fast path + expose the differ's content digest

## Context

goatherd-runtime's `Sandbox.Capture` contract requires: *a capture of
unchanged content at an unchanged timeline position must be digest-stable —
two captures of an identical workspace must produce equal WorkspaceState
digests* (settlement's `select` precondition compares them). That is the
Shepherd digest-stability concept: the carrier's state identity is
content-derived (the Python reference's git identities are), so digest
comparison is content comparison.

Croft cannot satisfy it today, and hosts cannot paper over it:

- `captureImpl` (`sandbox.go:702-758`) unconditionally mints a new sequence
  number and `snap.Commit`s a fresh layer — even when the active layer has
  **zero changes** vs its parent. Re-capturing identical content yields a new
  `SnapshotKey`.
- Croft is deliberately digest-free ("identity, not content equality"); the
  four-field struct hash croft-broker computes inherits the instability,
  because the *inputs* differ on every capture.

## Plan

1. **No-change fast path in `captureImpl`**: diff the active layer against its
   parent (the differ path already exists); if the change set is empty, skip
   `Commit`/`pinState`/`advance` and return the parent's committed state
   identity (restart the task on the unchanged active layer). Unchanged
   content at an unchanged position then returns the *same* state — stability
   by construction. Fork equality falls out for free: a child that applies a
   parent state and captures unchanged content returns the parent's identity.
2. **Surface the content digest**: `diffBlob`/`diffBlobBetween`
   (`diff.go:291,330`) already return an `ocispec.Descriptor` — containerd's
   differ output is content-addressed by construction. Compute and persist the
   committed layer's diff-blob digest (vs the empty base) and expose it, e.g.
   `WorkspaceState.ContentDigest`, so identity can be content equality for
   hosts that want it.
   - Migration note: a fifth field changes the four-field struct
     `snapshotState(...)` produces — croft-broker's sha256 scheme must be
     versioned/migrated when it picks this up.
3. **Moved-timeline nuance** (document, don't fight): the runtime contract
   *intentionally* digests a content-identical-but-moved workspace
   differently (select treats it as moved; apply merges). With `ParentKey` in
   the identity that falls out naturally — write it down.

## Acceptance

- Two captures of unchanged content at the same position return equal
  identity (unit + live).
- The fast path emits no new committed snapshot (assert on the fake
  snapshotter's commit count).
- Fork property: parent captures S; a second sandbox applies S and captures
  unchanged → S again.
- `ContentDigest` matches the daemon differ's blob digest (live test).
- croft-broker's digest scheme updated in step with the field addition.

## References

- yaah bead `yaah-kit` (container-lane seam work this unblocks)
- `croft-shepherd-fit.md` §8 (Frameworks dir) — gap analysis
- goatherd-runtime `sandbox/sandbox.go` `Capture` contract comment
notes:
Implemented on feat/croft-dlb (pushed, 926ee71): no-change capture fast path returns the remembered state verbatim (no commit), Apply remembers the caller's state so the fork property holds, and ContentDigest is exposed opt-in (Config.ContentDigest / WithContentDigest) as the differ's rootfs-relative blob digest. Content-digest diffs use their own lease purpose and no blob lease. Tests: fast path emits no commit, fork property, ContentDigest equals the differ digest and survives the fast path. Remaining: live daemon assertion for ContentDigest, croft-broker digest-scheme migration, and tagging v0.9.0.
Tagged v0.9.0 at 926ee71 and pushed; goatherd-runtime#21 resolves it and passes. If the PR is squashed, re-cut the tag on the merged commit.

title: v0.8.0 does not compile on Windows: syscall.O_NOFOLLOW in writeFileViaStaging
description:
# v0.8.0 does not compile on Windows: syscall.O_NOFOLLOW in writeFileViaStaging

## Context

`goatherd-croft v0.8.0` fails to build for `GOOS=windows`:

```
goatherd-croft@v0.8.0/sandbox.go:1194:75: undefined: syscall.O_NOFOLLOW
```

The call site is `writeFileViaStaging` — the argv-free write path that
`Config.StagingDir` enables:

```go
fd, err := os.OpenFile(staged, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
```

`O_NOFOLLOW` is defense in depth there (the comment says so): `O_EXCL` already
refuses to follow a pre-planted symlink, and the random name makes collisions
negligible. Windows defines no equivalent constant.

Verified separately, so the scope is exact and not guessed:

- `syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` — **undefined** on Windows. A minimal `GOOS=windows`
  program referencing it fails with the error above.
- `syscall.SIGKILL` (`client.go:806`, `:915`, `:928`) — **fine** on Windows; Go
  defines it as a pseudo-signal there. These are not part of the problem.

So this is a single-constant portability break, not a pervasive Unix dependency
in the code.

## Why it went unnoticed

- **Croft's CI is `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, single platform.** Nothing has ever
  compiled this library for Windows or macOS.
- **Build tags exist only on `live_*_test.go`.** No library file carries a
  `//go:build` constraint, so croft is Unix-only *in fact* while declaring
  itself platform-neutral. A consumer gets `undefined: syscall.O_NOFOLLOW`
  rather than the honest "build constraints exclude all Go files".
- **The code is new.** `Config.StagingDir` and `writeFileViaStaging` landed in
  **v0.7.0**. Confirmed against the module cache: `croft@v0.3.0` contains no
  `O_NOFOLLOW`, no `writeFileViaStaging`, and no `StagingDir`.

## Blast radius

Any consumer on Windows that upgrades past v0.7.0 breaks at compile time.

Already observed: **goatherd-runtime's CI runs a three-OS matrix**
(`ubuntu`/`macos`/`windows`) and iterates every nested module with
`go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`. Adding
`goatherd-runtime/sandbox/croft` — which pins croft v0.8.0 — turned
`test (windows-latest)` red at the nested-modules step, on a `main` that was
green. Tag run `40456627345`, tag `sandbox/croft/v0.1.0`.

Pending: **yaah.** Its CI matrix includes `windows-latest`, and
`.github/workflows/release-please.yml` cross-builds `{goos: windows,
goarch: amd64}` as a release artifact. yaah is green today *only* because it
pins the pre-rename `github.com/buchenberg/croft v0.3.0`, which predates the
offending code. yaah bead `yaah-kit` Phase 1 drops that pin and requires the
adapter (bringing croft v0.8.0+) — so this breaks yaah's Windows build and its
Windows release artifact the moment that lands.

**Downstream mitigation already in place:** `goatherd-runtime/sandbox/croft`
now gates its croft-importing files `//go:build linux` and provides a
non-importing stub (`backend_other.go`) for every other platform, exposing the
same `Config`/`Sandbox`/`New` surface with `New` returning
`ErrUnsupportedPlatform` and no backend registered. Hosts going *through the
adapter* therefore compile and ship on Windows and macOS. That contains the
problem for adapter consumers; it does nothing for anyone importing croft
directly on Windows.

## The decision needed

Croft is Linux-shaped by nature — overlayfs snapshots, bind mounts, client-side
FIFOs, a `/bin/sh -c "sleep infinity"` init process. But it already carries
`Microsoft/hcsshim` and `Microsoft/go-winio` as indirect deps via containerd, so
Windows containers are not inconceivable. Which is it?

- **Option A — declare Linux-only.** Add `//go:build linux` to the library
  files. Consumers then get "build constraints exclude all Go files", which
  names the real constraint instead of a missing constant. Cost: every consumer
  must gate its own imports (as the adapter now does), and any future Windows
  container support is a reversal.
- **Option B — stay portable, guard the constant.** Split the flag behind
  build-tagged files (`openflags_unix.go` / `openflags_other.go`), and on
  Windows either drop `O_NOFOLLOW` (relying on `O_EXCL` + the random name, which
  is what already carries the guarantee) or refuse `Config.StagingDir` outright.
  Cost: a second code path for a feature whose threat model is a bind-mounted
  staging dir — which Windows containers may not even have.
- **Option C — either way, add Windows to croft's CI matrix.** A `GOOS=windows
  go build ./...` step is nearly free and would have caught this at v0.7.0
  instead of two repos downstream. This is not an alternative to A or B; it is
  what stops the next one.

Recommendation: **A + C** — croft's substrate genuinely is Linux, so declaring
it is honest and makes consumers' build gates meaningful; C prevents a repeat.
Left open deliberately, because the answer depends on whether Windows container
support is ever intended, which is a roadmap question rather than a bug fix.

## Acceptance

- `GOOS=windows go build ./...` and `GOOS=darwin go build ./...` either succeed
  or fail with a build-constraint message that names Linux, not
  `undefined: syscall.O_NOFOLLOW`.
- croft's CI compiles for Windows and macOS (build + vet at minimum), so a
  future Unix-only constant cannot land unnoticed.
- The chosen platform story is recorded in croft's docs, and
  `goatherd-runtime/sandbox/croft` is revisited: if croft declares `//go:build
  linux`, the adapter's own gate becomes redundant belt-and-braces and its
  `backend_other.go` stub can be simplified or dropped.
- yaah-kit Phase 1 re-checked against the outcome, since yaah's Windows release
  artifact depends on it.

## References

- `sandbox.go:1189-1194` (the comment and the call site)
- CHANGELOG v0.7.0 (`Config.StagingDir`, argv-free staging writes)
- goatherd-runtime bead `shepherd-runtime-go-78r` (the adapter; its CI surfaced this)
- yaah bead `yaah-kit` Phase 1 (the pin drop this would break)
- goatherd-runtime CI run `40456627345`, tag `sandbox/croft/v0.1.0`

title: Decide the container-tier authority vocabulary: writable-roots shaping and broker egress
description:
# Decide the container-tier authority vocabulary: writable-roots shaping and broker egress

## Context

Shepherd's authority concept: **grants compile to writable roots, enforced at
the boundary**, plus egress postures (`allow_all` / `deny_all` / `broker` with
a pinned port). Croft's container boundary is currently binary:

- The whole container rootfs is writable. `Config.Secrets` are read-only bind
  mounts; there is no writable sibling and no read-only-rootfs option, so a
  `ConfinementSpec`'s writable-root set cannot lower into a container.
- `Config.validateNetwork` (`sandbox.go:227-236`) accepts only `""`/`"none"`
  (loopback-only) and `"host"` — mapping to `deny_all` and `allow_all`
  respectively. The `broker` posture has no container-tier answer, and
  Landlock cannot cover it inside a container whose seccomp profile may block
  the Landlock syscalls.

This is a **design decision before it is an implementation**: should the
container tier speak grant-shaped authority, or stay a coarse boundary tier
that fails loudly on unsupported postures?

## Option A — shaped authority

- `Config.Writable []string`: read-only rootfs + explicit writable bind
  mounts (the writable mirror of `Secrets`). A `ConfinementSpec`'s writable
  roots then lower into the container.
- `Network: "broker"` posture: a netns-local allowlist proxy for the pinned
  port.
- Enables per-binding grants in container sessions; more moving parts; new
  failure modes (mount ordering, proxy lifecycle).

## Option B — coarse but honest

- Keep the binary boundary; document the posture mapping
  (loopback = `deny_all`, host = `allow_all`).
- Refuse `broker` loudly in container sessions (config error, not silent
  downgrade) — fail-closed vocabulary.
- Authority stays whole-workspace ReadWrite in this tier — the container-mode
  instance of the granularity gap yaah's audit already tracks (§5.2 item 2).

## Recommendation

Decide against yaah's roadmap: if container sessions should ever honor
per-binding grants (e.g. multi-binding tasks in the container lane), Option A
is required; if the container lane remains the "strong boundary, coarse
grant" tier and granular authority stays on the syscall tier, Option B is
cheaper and honest. Record the decision in `docs/` (ADR-style) either way.

## Acceptance

- Decision recorded with rationale in croft docs.
- Chosen option implemented (A) or the tier boundary documented and the
  unsupported posture refused loudly (B), with tests either way.
- goatherd-runtime `sandbox/croft` adapter plan (see yaah bead `yaah-kit`
  Phase 0) updated to match the chosen vocabulary.

## References

- yaah bead `yaah-kit` (container-lane seam work)
- `croft-shepherd-fit.md` §6/§8 (Frameworks dir) — composition and gap analysis
- yaah-shepherd-gap-report §5.2 items 1-2 (authority granularity, macOS/advisory)

title: Decide whether croft stays a standalone repo or folds into goatherd-runtime
description:
# Decide whether croft stays a standalone repo or folds into goatherd-runtime

## Status: deferred deliberately (2026-10-27)

Raised while starting yaah-kit Phase 1, after the `sandbox/croft` adapter hit
real friction. The question: would it be easier to rewrite croft as a goatherd
sandbox *inside* goatherd-runtime than to keep translating to a standalone
library?

**Decision: no, not now.** Continue with the adapter. Revisit when the
conditions below change.

## Why the adapter stays

- **croft-broker is an independent consumer.** 2,241 lines, pinning
  `goatherd-croft v0.8.0` (local `replace => ../goatherd-croft`), using six
  symbols: `Config`, `New`, `Sandbox`, `ExecRequest`, `ExecResult`,
  `WorkspaceState`. Folding croft into the runtime forces the broker to depend
  on the runtime repo or fork. This is the decisive argument.
- **Dependency weight is the reason the nested module exists.** croft pulls
  containerd v2.3.5, errdefs, go-digest, image-spec, runtime-spec, plus
  hcsshim / go-winio / cgroups-v3 indirectly — 14,352 lines across 8 library
  files plus tests. That is exactly what the runtime core's kernel-plus-stdlib
  policy excludes. Folding it in as a first-class package undoes the firewall;
  folding it in as a nested module reproduces what the adapter already is.
- **The friction is croft-side design, not packaging.** The Windows
  `O_NOFOLLOW` break (`croft-itw`), sequence-keyed states defeating digest
  stability (`croft-dlb`), `Diff` without `maxLines`, the removed
  `StateKeyDeltaPatch` state model (`yaah-vlwm`) — a rewrite relocates all of
  these and dissolves none, while re-earning 14k lines of containerd
  integration and a live daemon test harness against a working released v0.8.0.
- **The adapter is small and already paid for.** ~300 lines of real
  translation, released as `sandbox/croft/v0.1.1`, CI green on three OSes,
  verified live against a real daemon.
- `croft-shepherd-fit.md` argues croft is a *world* on the substrate axis with
  carriers behind a seam so the framework stays dep-light. Inlining collapses
  the separation that document makes the case for.

## The variant worth naming

Fold croft into the runtime repo as the nested module's *implementation* rather
than a translation layer, retiring the standalone repo. This genuinely buys two
things:

1. **One version stream** — kills the skew risk yaah-kit lists, and which yaah
   is currently suffering from (pinned at the pre-rename v0.3.0 with removed
   API).
2. **Runtime CI conventions from day one** — the three-OS matrix is why the
   Windows portability break was caught at all; croft's own ubuntu-only CI let
   it ship unnoticed in v0.7.0.

Not done now because it does not unblock yaah-kit any faster: yaah must migrate
off the v0.3.0 API either way.

## Conditions that would reopen this

- **croft-broker is retired**, or the runtime becomes croft's only consumer —
  the standalone repo then loses its justification and folding in becomes
  clearly right.
- **Version skew bites again** after yaah-kit lands — i.e. the "bump the
  adapter with croft minors" discipline in yaah-kit's Risks section proves
  unworkable in practice.
- `croft-dlb`, `croft-ku0` and `croft-itw` all settle, so croft's design is
  stable enough that a move would not be chasing a moving target.

## Acceptance

- This bead stays open until one of the conditions above is met; it is a
  recorded deferral, not a rejected idea.
- When revisited, the deciding facts to re-check are: does croft-broker still
  exist and still consume croft directly; how many version-skew incidents
  happened since; and whether croft's open design beads have closed.

## References

- goatherd-runtime `sandbox/croft` v0.1.1 (the adapter), PR #17
- goatherd-croft beads `croft-dlb`, `croft-ku0`, `croft-itw`, `croft-jqp`
- yaah beads `yaah-kit` (Phase 1 migration), `yaah-vlwm` (the state-model
  regression that prompted this question)
- `croft-shepherd-fit.md` (Frameworks dir) — the two-axes analysis
